newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GERMAN PROSECUTORS DROP APPEAL IN GRAF CASE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GERMAN PROSECUTORS DROP APPEAL IN GRAF CASE.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Tuesday they had dropped an appeal against a jail sentence imposed on the father of tennis star Steffi Graf for tax evasion, meaning that the verdict against him was now legally binding.

Peter Graf was sentenced to three years and nine months jail in January after he was convicted on six counts of actual and attempted tax evasion on Steffi's earnings, but walked free pending the result of the appeals process.
"Mannheim prosecutors have withdrawn their appeal against the verdict of the Mannheim court in the case against Peter Graf," prosecutors said in a statement.
"After his defence lawyers also announced the withdrawal of their legal measure, the verdict against Peter Graf is legally binding."
Graf has already served 15 months in investigative custody during the investigation and subsequent trial.
It was not clear whether he would immediately have to return to prison or how long he might have to serve.
